ai.description: This 25–30 mm frog has a bright yellow belly and a brownish-green dorsum. It is distinguished by a prominent white spot on the snout and granular skin texture. Family: Rhacophoridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes flaviventris* is best distinguished by the vibrant, uniform lemon-yellow coloration on its belly and the undersides of its limbs, which lacks any dark mottling.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes flaviventris* inhabits the canopy and understory of evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Malabar bubble-nest frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the foliage of the Western Ghats' canopy and understory.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes flaviventris* undergoes direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in arboreal nests.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes flaviventris* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily found in the states of Karnataka and Kerala at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Malabar Bubble-nest Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps, typically heard from vegetation in moist evergreen forests during the monsoon.
